extraction.Name: Ben Conroy
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee, but took it on the advice of the Superintendent and the Farmer, who told him that if he did not take the patent and pay the taxes that he would lose the land
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Joe Skinner of Gordon, Nebr. for $1000.00; sold for an additional $300.00 and 4 lots and a house in Batesland, So. Dak. all being valued at about $250.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: could not pay the taxes so he mortgaged the land to Joe Skinner of Gordon, Nebr. for $1000.00; could not pay the taxes that were again assessed so he had to sell his land
extraction.Occupation/Income: makes his living by common labor, making about $400.00 per year
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent and in fair health; has a wife and four minor children to support; all he has is the four lots in Batesland where he lives and has not paid taxes on them since he got them; does not think the sale price was fair but it was the best he could do; the Government, State or County has contributed nothing to his aid since the patent was issued; subscribed and sworn before notary on November 30, 1928; County of Shannon, State of South Dakota | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
